title: reserve-buffering-plan-hosted-api-q2-2027
content:
Executive summary:

This working sheet defines a conservative, adaptive reserve-buffering strategy for the Hosted API fleet through Q2 2027. Goal: ensure customer latency SLOs remain met during unexpected peak spikes while minimizing wasted committed GPU capacity. Deliverables in this doc: per-region peak projections (tokens/sec and QPS), recommended headroom targets (static + adaptive components), buffer allocation algorithm, runway timeline for provisioning, and specific short-term action items.

Context and motivation:
- Recent traffic patterns show heavier burstiness after several product launches and increased adoption of streaming chat. Weekday 95th-percentile sessions are increasing faster than median (95/50 ratio grew from 2.1 -> 2.6 in last 6 months).
- We want a predictable, auditable policy that: (a) avoids last-minute overprovisioning, (b) preserves margin for 99th percentile spikes, and (c) enables aggressive autoscaling with cost-awareness.

Key assumptions (inputs used below):
- Model mix: 60% Llama-3-70b-q4f16 (baseline), 30% Llama-3-13b, 10% smaller models for embeddings and rerank.
- Effective sustained tokens/sec per H100-80GB slot serving Llama-3-70b-q4f16 (with batching+KV caching): 28,000 tokens/sec. For A100-80GB conservative: 18,000 tokens/sec.
- Average tokens per API call: 220 tokens (includes user prompt + model response).
- Avg QPS per token workload = tokens/sec / 220.
- Prefix/KV cache hit reduces token processing by 18% on high-repeat workloads; assumed global hit 12% during peak baseline; we run two scenarios (with/without elevated cache hits).
- Target reliability envelope: service should be able to handle 99th percentile 30-minute rolling peak plus an emergency 10-minute burst of 1.35x above that without customer-impacting degradation (fall back to quantized variant if necessary).

Buffering policy (two components):
1) Static baseline headroom: +22% of projected 95th-percentile peak per region (covers predictable diurnal+weekly variation).
2) Adaptive surge buffer: additional capacity sized to cover tail risk to 99th percentile and a short emergency burst. This is computed as max(12% of 95th, 10 GPUs worth), then scaled by model mix and region.
Rationale: static baseline avoids constant autoscale thrash; adaptive buffer buys time for cold scaling or cross-region spill.

Per-region projection table (scenario: May 2027 expected peak day):
- US-WEST (primary fleet): projected 95th tokens/sec = 820,000. Static headroom (22%) = 180,400. Adaptive buffer = 12% of 95th => 98,400 (rounded up to capacity equal to 4 H100 slots). Total reserve target = 820k + 180.4k + 98.4k = 1,099,000 tokens/sec (rounded).
- US-EAST: projected 95th tokens/sec = 540,000. Static headroom = 118,800. Adaptive buffer (min 2 H100) => 64,800. Total = 723,600 tokens/sec.
- EU-WEST: projected 95th tokens/sec = 360,000. Static headroom = 79,200. Adaptive buffer (min 2 H100) => 43,200. Total = 482,400 tokens/sec.
- APAC-SE: projected 95th tokens/sec = 200,000. Static headroom = 44,000. Adaptive buffer (min 2 A100 equiv => 36,000). Total = 280,000 tokens/sec.

Notes on GPU conversion and slot math used above:
- We assume H100 slot = 28k tokens/sec baseline. A100 slot = 18k tokens/sec. Adaptive buffer minimums are expressed in GPUs to avoid tiny fractional slices that complicate autoscaler policies.

Global totals and QPS equivalents (rounded):
- Projected global 95th tokens/sec = 1,920,000. Total reserve target (sum totals above) = ~2,585,000 tokens/sec.
- Equivalent QPS at avg 220 tokens/call: 2,585,000 / 220 ≈ 11,750 QPS.
- Equivalent 95th QPS = 1,920,000 / 220 ≈ 8,730 QPS.

Runway and provisioning guidance:
- Immediate (0-2 weeks): allocate reserve pool of 120 H100-equivalent slots across US-WEST and US-EAST (70/50 split) to cover static + adaptive buffers above while we validate traffic. For accounting: treat APAC reserve as A100-equivalent until H100 capacity is available in region.
- Mid-term (2-8 weeks): instrument new quantization-fallback policy and automate cross-region spillover tests. Add autoscaler hysteresis: 90s scale-up, 20m cooldown to limit oscillation during diurnal swings.
- Long-term (2-6 months): re-evaluate per-GPU tuning after quantized model variance improvements and updated kernel optimizations. Target to reduce static headroom from 22% -> 16% if sustained KV cache hit >18% for two months.

Operational playbook (short form):
- Detection: if tokens/sec > projected 95th + static headroom for 5 minutes, alert SRE and trigger auto-burst to adaptive buffer pool.
- Fallback ladder: 1) spill to cross-region reserve pools (same model family), 2) route new requests to quantized variant with latency warning header, 3) enforce per-customer QoS caps if needed.
- Telemetry: create per-route 1m and 10m rolling windows for tokens/sec, token latency P50/P95/P99, and cache-hit rate.

Cost tradeoffs and sizing rationale:
- Static headroom tuned conservative to avoid frequent customer-visible throttles during normal peak events. Adaptive buffer intentionally small but in multiples of GPUs to speed allocation decisions.
- Example cost snapshot (monthly run-rate incremental for reserves): 120 H100 slots reserved ~ equivalent to $X (placeholder) — finance to replace with committed pricing. Decision point: buy partial committed capacity vs on-demand depending on 3-month forecast horizon.

Open questions / risks:
- Model throughput assumptions: 28k tokens/sec per H100 is optimistic if next-gen attention kernels regress on some Llama-3 variants. Need microbenchmarks on production model builds (Marcus).
- Cache hit sensitivity: if real cache hits drop below 8% under new product traffic, static headroom may need +6pp.
- Cross-region legal limits: some customers cannot be served outside region; reserve planning must honor data locality for those tenants.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Run end-to-end load sim with 70% 70b mix on H100 and A100 images (Ben) — ETA 2027-04-18.
- Create telemetry dashboards for per-route tokens/sec 1m/10m (Rosa) — ETA 2027-04-20.
- Provision 120 H100-equivalent reserve pool across US-WEST/EAST (Infra ops) — ETA 2027-04-25.
- Draft customer communication template for quantized-fallback mode (GTM + Support) — ETA 2027-05-05.

Appendix: quick sizing math examples
- To cover 180,400 tokens/sec static headroom in US-WEST on H100s: 180,400 / 28,000 ≈ 6.44 -> allocate 7 H100 slots.
- Adaptive buffer 98,400 tokens/sec -> 98,400 / 28,000 ≈ 3.51 -> allocate 4 H100 slots.

This doc is a working draft. Please comment inline with microbenchmark outputs and updated committed-pricing numbers so we can convert placeholders to final cost model and move to review.
